title: Ballot measures on members' own pay or benefits, funded by the union's committees
question: Which ballot measures about members' retirement, staffing or pay did a City union's committees spend on?
finding: 4 such measures are among the unions' largest targets, $1.8 million in all; largest: Firefighters Local 798 $1.6 million for “Measure H: RETIREMENT BENEFITS FOR FIREFIGHTERS”; SEIU Local 1021 $122,000 for “Measure I: Retirement Benefits for Nurses and 911 Operators”; Police Officers Association $100,000 for “Measure F: Police Staffing and Voluntary Deferred Retirement: Option Program for the Police Department”.
how: Each union family's largest targets in the “unions” results (committee spending for or against a candidate or measure) whose name mentions retirement, pensions, benefits, staffing, salary, pay or wages.
limits: Unions may campaign on their members' pay; voters decide. the “unions” results keeps only each family's largest targets, so smaller measures are missing, and a few targets are outside San Francisco. What each measure cost the City is in the Controller's statement in the voter guide, not on disk.
